'''Helena Aksela''' (born 1947,<ref name="akat"/> [[Perho]]) is a Finnish physicist<ref name="Kaleva">[http://kirjastolinkit.ouka.fi/kaleva/elo07/6483969.xml Kaleva 7.8.2000] visited 20.7.2018</ref> and emeritus professor at the [[University of Oulu]].<ref>[http://www.oulu.fi/fysiikka/henkilokunta/aksela-helena Oulun yliopisto] visited 20.7.2018</ref> She was the first woman to be appointed a professor of physics in Finland.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.hs.fi/ihmiset/art-2000003886284.html|title=YLIOPISTOT: Ensimmäinen fysiikan naisprofessori nimitettiin|date=2000-05-26|work=Helsingin Sanomat|access-date=2018-07-25|language=fi-FI}}</ref>

Aksela gained her doctorate from the University of Oulu in 1980. The electron spectroscopy group led by Aksela was, in the 1990s, one of the first groups to experimentally apply the [[Auger effect|Auger]] resonant Raman effect.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kilpua |first1=Emilia |author2=Johanna Männistö |author3=Marko Huttula |title=Elektronispektroskopian tutkija ja Suomen ensimmäinen fysiikan naisprofessori Helena Aksela |url=https://blogs.helsinki.fi/sfs-70/2018/01/16/elektronispektroskopian-tutkija-ja-suomen-ensimmainen-fysiikan-naisprofessori-helena-aksela/ |website=Tarinoita Suomalaisista Fyysikoista |access-date=3 November 2018}}</ref> She was named a professor at the University of Oulu in 2000, in the field of [[Atomic, molecular, and optical physics|atomic and molecular physics]].<ref name="Kaleva"/> In 2001 she was appointed Academy Professor.<ref>{{Cite book|url=http://www.aka.fi/globalassets/awanhat/documents/tiedostot/julkaisut/annual-report-2001-pdf.pdf|title=Annual Report 2001|publisher=Academy of Finland|year=2002|isbn=951-715-386-4|location=Helsinki|pages=56}}</ref> Later she has worked in the department of physical sciences [[electron spectroscopy]] research group.<ref>[http://www.kaleva.fi/teemat/luonto/valon-ja-aineen-vuorovaikutus/232151/ Valon ja aineen vuorovaikutus, Kaleva.fi 9.10.2005] visited 24.7.2018</ref> She was a member of the [[Academy of Finland]] Research Council for Natural Sciences and Engineering from 2007 to 2009.<ref>{{Cite book|url=http://www.aka.fi/globalassets/awanhat/documents/tiedostot/julkaisut/annualreport2008_en_lr.pdf|title=Annual Report 2008|publisher=Academy of Finland|year=2009|isbn=978-951-715-720-9|location=Helsinki|pages=32}}</ref>

Aksela was made a Fellow of the [[Finnish Physical Society]] in 2013, based on her pioneering research work involving [[photoemission spectroscopy]] with [[synchrotron]]s, and associated researcher training, in addition to her active role in science politics.<ref>[http://www.fyysikkoseura.fi/fellow2.html Suomen fyysikkoseura.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170116161915/http://www.fyysikkoseura.fi/fellow2.html |date=2017-01-16 }} visited 24.7.2018</ref>

Aksela is married to professor [[Seppo Aksela]].<ref name="Kaleva"/>

==Awards and recognition==
* Award of the Pentti Kaitera fund, 2004<ref>[http://www.oulu.fi/university/professor-pentti-kaitera-fund Professor Pentti Kaitera fund] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180724154042/http://www.oulu.fi/university/professor-pentti-kaitera-fund |date=2018-07-24 }} visited 24.7.2018</ref>
* [[Finnish Academy of Science and Letters]] member from 2002<ref name="akat">[http://www.acadsci.fi/suomalainen-tiedeakatemia/jasenet/kotimaiset-jasenet.html Kotimaiset jäsenet. Suomalainen tiedeakatemia 31.10.2016.] visited 24.7.2018</ref>
* [[Theodor Homén Prize]] in 2019, awarded by the Finnish Academy of Science and Letters<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://researchportal.helsinki.fi/en/publications/sphinx-%C3%A5rsbok-vuosikirja-yearbook-2018-2019 |title=Sphinx: Årsbok - Vuosikirja - Yearbook 2018-2019 |date=2019 |publisher=Finska Vetenskaps-Societeten |isbn=978-951-653-435-3 |series=Sphinx |location=Helsinki|pages=217-218}}</ref>
